evidence.OBSERVED.plain: A published figure attributable to a named official source document.
evidence.ESTIMATED.plain: Derived from observed data. The method is named and the number of transformation steps is shown.
evidence.SUPPORTING.plain: Real observed data, shown for context. It is not a demand or supply measure.
evidence.UNAVAILABLE.plain: This number does not exist and cannot currently be computed. The reason is given.
evidence.vsUnavailable: "Estimated" means the number exists but was derived. "Unavailable" means it does not exist and cannot currently be computed.
confidence.label: Confidence
confidence.MEDIUM.plain: Derived from observed data through one documented transformation.
confidence.LOW.plain: Derived through more than one transformation, or resting on a historical or proxy structure.
confidence.notNumeric: Confidence is a category, never a percentage or probability.

landing.heading: What this tells you, and what it does not
landing.whatItIs: This system shows where relative labour-demand signals are higher, at what confidence, over what coverage, and from which sources.
landing.whatItIsNot: It does not publish a demand-supply gap. It does not publish a shortage or a forecast, and it publishes no occupation-level supply figure. Those capabilities are reported as explicitly unavailable, each with a reason and the evidence that would unblock it.
landing.noTotal: No national total labour-demand figure is published. The measure is cumulative NCS vacancy registrations since inception, and most of it is not geographically attributable.
national.heading: National overview
national.observedNote: Vacancy counts as published. The NCS-sector to NIC-section alignment is the project's own.
national.estimatedNote: An estimated split of observed industry totals across NCO-2015 divisions, using an ILOSTAT/PLFS industry × occupation structure. Confidence varies by row.
state.heading: State view
state.trainingNote: Candidate counts within a named scheme and period. These are not a supply quantity: no occupation or trade dimension exists.
state.residualExcluded: The PAN-India residual is excluded from this comparison and disclosed separately. It is never allocated to a state or district.

occupation.heading: Occupation view
occupation.districts: Districts within a state, for this division
occupation.informative: Across districts within one state and one division, this ordering combines the enterprise and occupation structures, so it restates neither input. It remains an estimated allocation signal.
derivation.heading: How this signal is derived
derivation.note: The datasets below are factors in this signal, not independent evidence for it.
methodology.heading: Methodology & evidence
methodology.gap: Why no demand–supply gap is published
methodology.gapBody: A numeric gap can only be computed where demand and a supply quantity are measured at the same geography, occupation grain, unit, period and population definition. No occupation-level or trade-level geographic supply quantity exists, and the joint distribution cannot be recovered from the marginals that do. This is a property of the evidence, not a modelling difficulty.
methodology.hybrid: Why the pressure indicator is experimental only
methodology.hybridBody: A hybrid demand-pressure / training-system indicator was designed but is not implemented or published. Its classification changes depending on which training scheme is read, so it is not a production output.
methodology.vintagesBody: Figures on this site come from five sources with different as-on dates. No single "data as of" date applies, and no trend may be drawn across them.
coverage.heading: Coverage & limitations
unavailable.heading: Unavailable capabilities
unavailable.intro: Each capability below is reported with its reason and the condition that would unblock it. None is hidden, and none is shown as zero.
reason.NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: Not identifiable — structural: the evidence cannot determine this, and more of the same data would not change that.
reason.NOT_ACQUIRED: Not acquired — the source exists but no snapshot has been taken.
reason.ACCESS_PENDING: Access pending — identified, but access is unresolved.
reason.NOT_AVAILABLE: Not available — not published at the grain required.
reason.NOT_SUPPORTED_YET: Not supported yet — blocked by a temporal condition, not a structural one.
reason.PROHIBITED: Prohibited — doing this would invent data.

legend.bar: Bar length is relative to the largest row in view; it carries no unit.
legend.rank: Rank is a position, not a quantity.
landing.points: Every figure is labelled — observed, estimated or context, so the label tells you how far it sits from a source document.
Coverage is published — you can see how much of the base a figure rests on before you act on it.
!What is missing is listed too — each blocked capability appears with its reason and the condition that would unblock it.
landing.steps: Pick a level in the left rail: national, state, district or occupation.
Read the panel's one-line description and its reading notes before the table.
Check the evidence strip above each table: tier, confidence, as-on date and source.
Export the rows if you need them; the export carries the same qualifiers as the screen.
national.lede: Observed sector figures, an estimated occupation split, and the labour-force context that frames them.
state.lede: One state's observed figure, the relative ordering of its districts, and its training-system outcomes.
district.lede: One district's relative signal, its position inside its own state, and its occupation detail where Census data exists.
occupation.lede: One NCO-2015 division: its estimated national composition, and the relative ordering of districts inside a chosen state.
methodology.lede: What each output measures, how it was derived, and why some capabilities are not published.

coverage.barredNote: These fields are withheld because the evidence does not support publishing them.
explain.industry.what: Vacancy registrations on the NCS portal, counted by sector exactly as the source publishes them.
explain.industry.points: Measure — Cumulative registrations since the portal's inception, not a monthly flow and not a stock of open posts.
Sector alignment — The NCS sector to NIC section match is the project's own; a blank NIC section means no match was published.
!Rows do not add to a national figure — rows flagged heterogeneous or residual span more than one sector.
explain.occcomp.what: An estimated split of the observed sector figures across NCO-2015 occupation divisions.
explain.occcomp.points: Measure — Lakh-equivalent estimates, derived from the observed sector totals rather than counted directly.
Method — The split applies an ILOSTAT/PLFS industry by occupation structure, so the structure is borrowed from elsewhere.
!Confidence varies by row — each row carries its own category, and a LOW row rests on more than one transformation.
explain.plfs.what: Labour-force participation from the Periodic Labour Force Survey, shown to frame the panels above.
explain.plfs.points: Role — Real observed survey data, included for context only. It is not a demand measure.
Grain — Published for India as a whole; no state or district breakdown is valid at this vintage.
!Not comparable with the sector panel — a different source, period and statistical basis.
explain.residual.what: Vacancies the source publishes without a single state, because the posting covers PAN-India or several states at once.
explain.residual.points: Why it stands alone — it is never divided among states or districts; doing so would invent a location the source does not give.
What it means for the rest — every state figure on this site is drawn from the remainder, so this share is the part no geography can claim.
explain.districts.what: A relative signal that orders the districts inside one state. It is not a count of anything.
explain.districts.points: Measure — Unitless and relative. The number answers 'which districts sit higher', never 'how many'.
How it is built — The observed state figure is distributed by each district's Udyam enterprise share, so the ordering inside a state is the Udyam ordering.
!Compare only inside one state — the signal is not comparable across state borders, and each bar is drawn against the largest row in view.
explain.training.what: Candidate counts inside one named scheme and period: enrolled, trained, assessed, certified and placed.
explain.training.points: Measure — Five distinct stages, kept apart. Certified is not the same as placed, and placed records the point of report only.
No occupation or trade dimension — these figures are not an occupation-level supply figure and cannot be set against the demand panels.
!NO_DATA is not zero — a dash in the source stays NO_DATA, because a dash does not state that nobody was counted.
explain.districtdetail.what: This district's relative signal, with the position it holds inside its own state.
explain.districtdetail.points: Rank — A position among the districts of this state only, out of that state's own count. It is not a national position.
Inputs — The observed state figure and the district's Udyam enterprise share; the panel below lists every factor used.
explain.districtocc.what: A relative signal ordering NCO-2015 occupation divisions inside this one district.
explain.districtocc.points: Measure — Relative within this district. It does not say how many people work in a division.
Structure borrowed from 2011 — occupation shares come from Census 2011 while the demand baseline is far more recent, so the two vintages do not line up.
!Unclassified workers are excluded, not redistributed — the excluded share is printed, so the rows do not account for the whole district.
explain.occnat.what: For the chosen NCO-2015 division, its estimated composition across NIC sections and NCS sectors.
explain.occnat.points: Conditional share — The share within this division, answering how the division is spread rather than how large it is.
!Estimated, not counted — the figures inherit the borrowed industry by occupation structure described on the methodology page.
explain.occdist.what: For one division and one state, a relative signal ordering that state's districts.
explain.occdist.points: Why this ordering is informative — it combines the enterprise structure with the occupation structure, so it restates neither input on its own.
!Districts without Census occupation data are left out of the list, never shown as zero.
explain.vintages.what: Each output carries its own as-on date, because the sources behind them were published years apart.
explain.vintages.points: Why no single date applies — the figures come from five sources whose as-on dates span more than a decade.
What to do with it — quote the vintage of the row you are reading, and never draw a trend across two sources.
explain.derivation.what: A derivation input is a dataset used as a factor inside a signal, not a second reading of the same thing.
explain.derivation.points: Example — The Udyam enterprise share is what distributes a state figure across districts, so it is a factor in that signal.
!Why the distinction matters — a factor cannot also be read as proof of the result it helped produce.
explain.peroutput.what: One entry per published output, read from the publication contract and the warehouse rather than written into this page.
explain.peroutput.points: Open any row — for its method, limitations, unit, measure basis, sources and prohibited readings.
Tier and status differ — the tier is the role an output plays; the evidence status is read from the data itself.
explain.coverage.what: How much of the published base each figure actually rests on, derived from the warehouse when this page loads.
explain.coverage.points: Why it is published — a figure without its coverage can be quoted far beyond what it supports.
Two domains — demand evidence and training evidence are counted separately and are not added together.
explain.quality.what: The pipeline's own contract checks, with the observed and expected value for each.
explain.quality.points: What a check is — an assertion the build must satisfy, such as a total reconciling to the figure its source prints.
Why it is on screen — a figure whose checks are not visible cannot be audited by the person using it.
explain.unavailable.what: Capabilities this system cannot compute are published here with their reasons, rather than hidden or shown as zero.
explain.unavailable.points: Reason code — says whether the block is structural, or only that a source has not been acquired yet.
Unblocking condition — names the gate that would have to be met; where the reason is structural, more of the same data would not change it.
!A blocked capability is not a zero — and not an empty table either; those three states are kept distinct everywhere.
tabs.label: Sections of this view
explain.statetotal.what: This state's share of the published NCS vacancy registrations, as the source reports it.
explain.statetotal.points: Measure — A cumulative count since the portal's inception, attributed to this state by the source itself.
!The PAN-India remainder is not included — it is disclosed separately and never divided among states.
